title: General biology II: evolution and physiology
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Explain evolution, population genetics and diversity, then the physiology of animal tissues, nervous, endocrine, musculoskeletal, circulatory, respiratory, digestive, excretory, immune and reproductive systems.

blocks.deliverable: Use the Hardy–Weinberg equation to estimate carrier frequency.
Compare bacterial, fungal and animal cells as drug targets.
Draw a negative-feedback loop for body temperature.
Week 7 midterm; explain hormone feedback with the thyroid as the example.
Trace a red blood cell through the heart and lungs.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Physiology case report: follow one meal from mouth to bloodstream to kidney, explaining each organ's role, with a labeled diagram.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
